newsitem.title: UK: HK should be bridge, not barrier to China - Cook.
newsitem.headline: HK should be bridge, not barrier to China - Cook.

text.p: Britain's new foreign secretary Robin Cook said on Friday Hong Kong should be a bridge and not a barrier between Britain and China after the colony is handed over to Beijing on June 30.
"The transfer of sovereignty at the midnight stroke marks not the end of Britain's engagement with Hong Kong and China but a new beginning," he wrote in the London Times.
The new Labour government has made human rights a top foreign policy priority. Cook said that after June 30, "foremost is an abiding commitment to the people of Hong Kong."
Cook, who will be flying with Prime Minister Tony Blair to Hong Kong for the handover ceremonies, said: "Hong Kong should be a bridge, not a barrier, between Britain and China."
He said Britain would ensure that the issue of a stable and free Hong Kong mattered to the international community.
The same applied on the domestic front. "We have agreed to report to parliament every six months on Hong Kong at least until the turn of the century," he said.
